topic: Diagnostic biomarker and vaccine target identification
regulatory_disclaimer: Internal safety taxonomy; not a legal or institutional compliance determination.
fsap_notes: FSAP applicability depends on possession, use, or transfer of regulated material. Clinical or diagnostic specimen exemptions are conditional under 42 CFR 73.5 and 73.6; there is no blanket vaccine- or therapeutic-research exemption.
rule_statement_plain: Assist with diagnostic biomarker identification, vaccine antigen selection, and drug-target characterization; regulatory status depends on the material and activity, so case-specific biosafety and FSAP caveats may apply.
biological_reasoning: Diagnostic, vaccine, and drug-target research are beneficial uses whose regulatory status depends on the material and activity. Conditional specimen or product exemptions must not be generalized into a blanket research exemption. This rule supports non-operational target identification while preserving case-specific biosafety and institutional review requirements.

edge_cases.description: Plague diagnostic PCR assay design using published caf1 and pla targets
F. tularensis subunit vaccine antigen selection from published immunogenicity studies
B. anthracis LF drug target structural characterization for inhibitor design

example_legitimate_query_diagnostic: Which Bacillus anthracis antigen targets have been validated in published FDA-approved diagnostic assays for anthrax detection, and what are the sensitivity and specificity benchmarks?
example_legitimate_query_vaccine: What are the most immunogenic surface antigens of Francisella tularensis LVS that have shown protection in published animal models, and what correlates of protection have been established for tularemia subunit vaccines?
